variant.label: Flat bench press, 120 kg · contact v2

model.name: Catelli v4 marker-enabled full-body squat model (Rajagopal/Lai lineage), derived copy
transformations: loaded the byte-identical marker-enabled Catelli v4 model
set appliesForce=false on every Force in the ForceSet (80 muscles, 17 coordinate actuators) so inverse dynamics sees gravity and external loads only
no barbell body: the bar is a rigid hand-carried load applied at both palms during inverse dynamics
Experimental contact-v2: pelvis tilt/height and leg posture solved for the fixed human back and lower pad surface; calibrated pad load stations replace bone-only references.
model.license_note: SimTK project page records an MIT use agreement; the derived model is generated locally and not redistributed.

assumptions: The static supine pelvis tilt and height are solved against the fixed fitted human back and glute/upper-thigh surface, with both feet replanted flat. Pad load resultants act at the calibrated contact x coordinates, on the pelvis and torso respectively; the same declared static-leg-weight/no-leg-drive support split is retained.

The bar follows an authored J-curve. Its lower-chest touch height is calibrated against the unchanged fitted display torso plus the shaft radius. Shoulder and elbow angles solve the fixed 75 mm analytical grasp station exactly; bar position, velocity and external hand loads use that same station. Elbow flare is a posture preference. This is contact-informed authored motion, not motion capture or a predictive muscle simulation.

The barbell (120 kg) is a rigid load carried at both palms with a 50/50 hand split; it keeps a horizontal axis and its inertial and gravitational load is applied at the palms during inverse dynamics. Lateral (medial/lateral) hand forces are not modelled.

The support is statically indeterminate between bench and feet; the declared split gives each foot the static weight of its own leg (no leg drive) and the bench the remainder through two pad contacts (glutes and upper back) with vertical shares from the sagittal moment balance. Where that balance would make the glute contact pull on the pad (the bar over the shoulders at lockout), the glutes leave the pad and the upper-back contact's centre of pressure moves headward along the pad to where the balance puts it, bounded by the top of the shoulders. Shoulder and elbow net moments do not depend on that split; the lumbar moment does.
The generic model has a 3-degree-of-freedom ball shoulder without scapular motion; shoulder moments are net moments about that joint, not glenohumeral or scapulothoracic loads.
Segment masses and inertias are the generic Catelli/Rajagopal values for a 75 kg lifter; no subject scaling was applied.
Muscles and coordinate actuators were disabled; results are net joint moments, not muscle, joint-contact, or spinal forces.

The same 1.25 m bench pad is placed with its foot end 0.15 m ahead of the pelvis so the thighs leave the pad naturally. Up to 2 mm of head-pad geometric overlap is treated as an unresolved foam-compression cue; pad compliance is not dynamically modelled. The rigid Catelli torso has no independent head coordinate.
At the touch the hands retain the full bar load; the chest is a geometric touch cue. No load-bearing chest support force or soft-tissue compliance model is included.
claims_boundary: Simulated lift: the kinematics are authored/solved and the external forces are model-derived, not measured. Net joint moments describe this simulation only. No muscle force, joint-contact force, spinal load, coaching, or injury-risk claim is made.

frames.axes: OpenSim ground frame: x forward (toward the lifter's feet when supine), y up, z to the lifter's right; body meshes and transforms share this convention

sign_notes.pelvis_tilt: +90 = flat supine, head toward -x; below 90 the hips lie lower than the lumbar joint (arch)

bar.force_note: force the lifter must apply to the bar: m_bar * (a_bar - g); equal and opposite to the load on the lifter
bar.hand_force_note: force the bar applies to each hand (half the bar load), applied at the palm station in inverse dynamics

ground_reaction.method: Newton-Euler balance of all model bodies plus the carried bar; the total support wrench is split by declaration between the feet (static leg weight) and the bench (remainder through the glute and upper-back contacts, the latter's centre of pressure moving headward when the glutes would otherwise pull)
ground_reaction.cop_note: for the bench press this point is the bench contact under the pelvis, not a floor centre of pressure
ground_reaction.split_assumption: each foot carries the static weight of its own leg (no leg drive); the bench takes the remainder through two pad contacts (glutes under the pelvis, upper back) whose vertical shares follow from the sagittal moment balance; where the glute share would be negative the glutes leave the pad and the upper-back centre of pressure moves headward, bounded by the top of the shoulders

upper_back.point_note: point is the shoulder-blade reference; points is the per-frame centre of pressure, which moves headward (toward the shoulders) whenever the glutes would otherwise pull on the pad

inverse_dynamics.method: opensim.InverseDynamicsSolver with finite-differenced speeds/accelerations; foot loads, half the bar load at each palm, and the two bench contact forces (pelvis, torso) applied through station/frame Jacobian transposes

residuals.meaning: Generalized forces left on the six pelvis-to-ground mobilities after the declared support split; near zero means the kinematics, inertia, and applied loads are mutually consistent.

path_screen.note: The legs are static in the bench press; the screen is reported for completeness.

contact_calibration.method: Upper envelope of the exact posed torso triangle surface expanded by the 14.5 mm shaft radius; lower-chest fore-aft touch location preserved.
contact_calibration.pad_contact_note: Fixed surface contact points are solved at the source touch arm posture, including the glute/upper-thigh seam. Symmetric pad resultants are applied to pelvis and torso as a declared coarse support model; skin weights are not a physical force-sharing model.

changes: Static pelvis posture and pad load stations recomputed against the fixed fitted human surface; feet replanted.
Bar touch height recomputed against the fixed fitted human surface.
The analytical grasp station is 75 mm from the wrist, consistently used by arm IK, bar kinematics and external hand loads.
Palm positions enforced as hard IK constraints; elbow flare remains a posture preference.
Coordinates, speeds, accelerations, bar loads, support wrench, moments and work recomputed by the preserved OpenSim pipeline.
